title: When a Set-Aside Runs Short: Shortfall Funding, Depletion and Charges Not Payable
content:
This servicing rule of Set-Aside Accounts governs which set-aside a bill may be paid from, what happens when a payable bill is larger than the balance, and when a set-aside becomes depleted.

## 1. Which set-aside pays

1.1 A bill is paid only from the set-aside on the same loan whose plan pays that charge type.
1.2 A bill for a charge the plan does not pay, or for homeowners-association dues, ground rent or a special assessment, is declined as not payable from this set-aside, and the charge stays the borrower's to pay. No plan pays homeowners-association dues, ground rent or special assessments.
1.3 A bill is paid from a set-aside only while the set-aside status is active, as the set-aside record shows before the payment.

## 2. Shortfall

2.1 When a payable bill exceeds the set-aside balance, the set-aside pays its entire remaining balance and no more.
2.2 The unpaid remainder is handled under the plan's shortfall setting:
- **Borrower billed, then corporate advance** — the borrower is billed for the remainder and, if the borrower has not paid it by the bill's due date, Cedarline pays it as a corporate advance under the property charge repayment rules.
- **Corporate advance** — Cedarline pays the remainder as a corporate advance at once.

## 3. Depletion

3.1 When a disbursement or fee draw brings the balance to 0.00, the set-aside becomes depleted on the same date.
3.2 The borrower is notified, within the plan's depletion notice period in calendar days, that the charges the set-aside paid are now the borrower's to pay.
3.3 A depleted set-aside pays nothing further.

## 4. Default protection

While a Fully Funded LESA pays a charge, a missed payment of that charge is never a borrower property-charge default.

## Worked case on hypothetical figures

| Input | Figure |
|---|---|
| Set-aside balance, status active | 700.00 |
| Payable tax installment on file | 1,000.00 |
| Paid from the set-aside | 700.00 (the whole balance, no more) |
| Unpaid remainder | 300.00 |
| Balance after payment | 0.00, so the set-aside is depleted on the payment date |

Under the "borrower billed, then corporate advance" setting the 300.00 is billed to the borrower and is advanced by Cedarline only if still unpaid on the bill's due date; under the "corporate advance" setting it is advanced at once.
